Backesc

While a question or a box is open, such as Mark everything read?, the keys belong to it. Tab moves between its buttons, ↵ or Space presses the highlighted one, and esc closes it. It opens on the button that does the thing, so A and then ↵ marks everything read. The list keys work again when it closes.

The app takes no key that is held with ⌘, ⌥ or Ctrl, except ⌘, (Ctrl+, off the Mac) for Configuration, ⌘+, ⌘− and ⌘0 (Ctrl off the Mac) for the text size, Ctrl with PgUp, PgDn, Home or End, and Alt with ↑ or ↓ on Linux and Windows. Alt with ← or → stays with the system. The other keys go to the system, so the window-arranging keys of macOS and the desktop-switching keys of Linux work while the app is in front.

On a Mac, ⌘W and the red button close the window, and the app stays in the Dock and goes on checking sources and summarizing. Click the Dock icon to open the window again. ⌘Q quits.
